day: Saturday of week 24 in Ordinary Time or Saint Januarius, Bishop, Martyr or Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary
text:
There is something tender in how Jesus speaks of seeds and soil. He does not scold the path or shame the rock or curse the thorns. He simply describes what happens when the word lands in different kinds of hearts, and the honest truth settles gently around us: we are all kinds of soil.

Yet Paul's letter reminds us that we are not fixed in what we are. A seed must die to become something new, something the naked eye cannot predict. We begin one way—earthly, perishable, weak—but we are being remade. The word of God works in us like that hidden dying and rising, turning us slowly toward the heavenly pattern we are meant to embody. What seems weak becomes powerful. What seems contemptible becomes glorious. The transformation happens not because we earn it, but because we let it happen, through our patience and perseverance.

Walk today in the presence of the living God, knowing that you are both the soil being tended and the seed being changed. If your heart feels rocky or tangled right now, that is not your final form. The word continues its patient work, turning you toward the light.
